title: Business Acquisition — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: A field workbook for buying, financing, and protecting a cash-flowing small business, from the buy-versus-build case through search, deal sourcing, SBA 7(a) lending, and the seller note bridge

worksheets.title: The Buy-Versus-Build Decision and First-Deal Readiness
worksheets.purpose: Turn the case for acquiring a cash-flowing small business into a written thesis, a target statement, and an opening-offer rule. Then set the non-negotiable gates on books, concentration, small-deal terms, and first-year operating discipline before any seller conversation begins.
instructions: Complete every field in writing before contacting a broker or owner; a thesis that exists only in your head will bend under deal pressure.
Anchor each answer to a specific practitioner number, such as the 2% SBA default rate or the 2.5-4.5x Main Street multiple.
Replace the sample figures with your own revenue band, multiple, geography, and timeline, and date the page when you finish.
Mark any field where your answer conflicts with an operator gate, and resolve that conflict before signing an LOI.
Revisit this worksheet every 30 days of search and record what changed, remembering that 90% of people who start looking never buy.

fields.name: buy_vs_build_case
fields.prompt: State in plain terms why buying a cash-flowing small business beats starting one for you, citing the failure and default comparisons, and name the specific personal risk you are trying to remove by acquiring instead of building from scratch.
fields.example: Startups fail at roughly 20% in year one, while acquisition loans default at about 2%, per Dallas M&A attorney Kevin Henderson [Kevin Henderson — YXFpxJrIjD0 @ 00:08:33]. My risk to remove is a zero-revenue first year; I want inherited customers, staff and cash flow on day one, and I accept that I am buying the business as it sits.

fields.name: return_benchmark
fields.prompt: Record the return benchmark you will hold every target against, comparing the average ETA return with public-market returns and with search fund versus venture loss rates, and write the minimum return that would justify your time and capital.
fields.example: Stanford data puts average ETA ROI at 34% against roughly 9-10% for the stock market [Joel Ankney — cl31TiHq92Y @ 00:06:23]. INSEAD cites about 20% partial loss and 10% total loss for search funds, with IRR of 25-35% versus 13-15% for VC [INSEAD — i7FBr84AUfY @ 00:07:55]. My floor: a deal must model at least 25% annual return on equity.

fields.name: multiple_arbitrage
fields.prompt: Write out the valuation multiple you expect to pay at your target size, compare it with larger-company multiples, and explain how the multiple gap creates value for you when you eventually grow, refinance, or sell the business you buy.
fields.example: Ruback and Yudkoff say the magic is in the multiples: $1M of EBITDA sells for about $4M, while $10M of EBITDA sells for $100M at 10x [Acquiring Minds — c1OtHjDpymM @ 00:07:37]. Deibel prices Main Street at 2.5-4.5x earnings against 19-28x for public companies [Jake & Gino — xpFa8hcRy_k @ 00:17:02]. I expect to pay near 4x cash flow on my first deal.

fields.name: target_statement
fields.prompt: Draft a one-paragraph target statement naming the revenue band, earnings multiple, industry traits, and geography you will pursue, plus the date by which you intend to be under LOI, so urgency and focus are written down before you search.
fields.example: Deibel says 90% of people who start looking never buy, blaming missing target statements and missing urgency, and notes a focused buyer could own a company within 6 months [DigitalTriggers — u2bZWIf9b5k @ 00:58:38]. Mine: $1-5M revenue, 2.5-4.5x earnings, cash flow and simplicity, not asset or capital intensive, within two hours of home, under LOI in six months.

fields.name: sourcing_channel_plan
fields.prompt: List the sourcing channels you will work each week, such as brokers, trade-show lists, direct outreach, and local in-person networking, and assign a weekly activity count to each so the plan can be audited rather than merely hoped for.
fields.example: Ruback says belly to belly sales beat national email campaigns, and one Houston searcher never had lunch alone [HBS Rock Center for Entrepreneurship — oJcm3Bn-lXE @ 00:46:43]. Deibel adds going straight to brokers lops off about two years [Jake & Gino — xpFa8hcRy_k @ 00:32:31]. Weekly plan: five broker calls, three owner lunches, twenty trade-show list contacts, and one Sabri curve listing review daily.

fields.name: opening_offer_rule
fields.prompt: Set your opening offer multiple, the concession you are prepared to give back, and the walk-away price, then explain how that concession preserves goodwill with the seller without destroying the economics that made the deal attractive at the start.
fields.example: Searcher Antonio opens at 2.5x, and Ruback advises giving back a quarter or half turn to keep goodwill, because if the deal is good at 3, it's still good [HBS Rock Center for Entrepreneurship — oJcm3Bn-lXE @ 00:57:40]. My rule: open at 2.5x, concede to 3x, walk above 3.5x, since price is the one term I control by walking.

fields.name: books_and_bank_gate
fields.prompt: Describe how you will verify that the target keeps one honest set of books, including how many months of bank statements you will reconcile and what finding would make you kill the deal or reprice it before closing.
fields.example: The gate is explicit: kill or reprice any target showing two sets of books, and do not close without 36 months of bank statements reconciled [Technically News — nOnsMlkLh10 @ 01:08:24]. I will request 36 months of statements from every account, tie deposits to reported sales by month, and walk if unexplained cash gaps exceed one month of revenue.

fields.name: referral_concentration_map
fields.prompt: Map the target's revenue by customer and by referral source, identify any single client or referrer controlling a large share of sales, and decide whether that concentration kills the deal or shifts risk back to the seller.
fields.example: A top-five client list routed through one referrer is a deal-killer, not a footnote [The Wall Street Skinny — MpeYmBDptXs @ 00:44:27]. The gate requires no single client above 10% of sales, or an earnout or seller note shifting risk back [Master Afle — LzJITHl_i2k @ 01:14:56]. My map flags one referrer driving 30% of revenue, so I reprice with an earnout or walk.

fields.name: small_deal_terms_to_strike
fields.prompt: List the NDA and LOI terms you will strike or refuse on a small deal, including commission clauses, deposits, breakage fees, and non-compete signatories, and record the exact language you will use when pushing back on each one.
fields.example: Joel Ankney strikes buyer-pays-commission NDA clauses, refuses deposits and breakage fees, and gets the founder to personally sign the non-compete [Joel Ankney — cl31TiHq92Y @ 00:20:09]. He pays no deposit under $5-6M, calls a deposit request a red flag, and labels breakage fees mid-market creep [Joel Ankney — cl31TiHq92Y @ 00:35:06]. My line: no deposit, no breakage fee, founder signs personally.

fields.name: day_one_people_plan
fields.prompt: Write your first-year operating plan for people and changes, including the freeze period on personnel moves, who owns each P&L line, which top customers you will meet before closing, and the salary you will draw at first.
fields.example: Freeze personnel changes for six months post-close and go drastic only if things hit the fan [Technically News — nOnsMlkLh10 @ 00:58:06]. Write a person's name next to every P&L line, book the top 20 paying customers before closing, and keep your salary low [Let's Buy a Business — WP5MdYhV05A @ 00:16:59]. My plan: six-month freeze, twenty customer meetings booked, owner salary under market.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when the target statement fits in one paragraph with a dated LOI deadline, the opening and walk-away multiples are written, the 36-month bank reconciliation and concentration gates are accepted in writing, and the day-one P&L ownership plan names a person for every line.

worksheets.title: Running the Search: Model, Funnel, and Origination Engine
worksheets.purpose: Choose a search model, budget the runway, and size the funnel. Then build the broker, outreach, and marketplace machinery that produces qualified owner conversations at a steady weekly volume, and screen out thin margins, bad data, and dishonest sellers early.
instructions: Pick traditional or self-funded search first, because the equity, runway, and budget answers all depend on that choice.
Translate every funnel benchmark into a weekly activity count you can audit on a calendar, not a quarterly hope.
Build outreach infrastructure before writing copy: lookalike domains, warmed mailboxes, and verified marketplace profiles come first.
Apply the 15% margin floor and the 85% data-accuracy gate before spending NDA, diligence, or hiring money.
Log every seller's stated reason for selling at each meeting, and compare the answers side by side before drafting any offer.

fields.name: search_model_choice
fields.prompt: Choose between a traditional investor-backed search and a self-funded search, recording the equity you would keep under each model, who carries the runway cost, and why the cost of outside capital is or is not worth it to you.
fields.example: Traditional searchers earn 20-30% equity in thirds, while self-funded searchers keep 60-73% but carry the runway themselves. One practitioner put the trade-off bluntly: I've never been able to deposit a percentage of common equity in the bank [Acquiring Minds — 0lg8Gh_uAPU @ 00:18:28]. I choose self-funded, with twelve months of personal runway already saved.

fields.name: search_capital_budget
fields.prompt: Build a search budget covering salary, travel, legal, diligence, and other costs for a two-year runway, compare it with typical traditional search raises, and record how many months you can fund before you must close or stop.
fields.example: Peter Harris puts the median traditional raise at $500-550K, typically $400-700K and $800-900K for two searchers, covering about two years of salary, interns, legal, travel, bankers and diligence [VCPete — i_Ownd9smbk @ 00:02:31]. My self-funded budget totals $160K: $120K salary-equivalent drawdown, $30K legal and diligence, $10K travel, funding eighteen months before a hard go-or-stop decision.

fields.name: funnel_targets
fields.prompt: Set numeric funnel targets from companies reviewed down to information memoranda, owner conversations, offers, and LOIs, using benchmark funnels as a reference, and write the weekly volume you need to reach one closed purchase on schedule.
fields.example: Pete Seligman's funnel ran about 200 companies to 50 IMs to 20 conversations to 5 offers to 1 purchase [David Nazeem Aboud — _exEOi-Wxuk @ 00:15:24]. Self-funded closers submitted 6.9 LOIs and had 2.4 executed [Acquiring Minds — KT5T3j2jVQ4 @ 00:45:01]. Over 40 weeks, I need five companies reviewed weekly, one owner conversation every two weeks, and an offer every eight weeks.

fields.name: broker_follow_up_cadence
fields.prompt: Describe your broker relationship system, including how you build the list, how often you follow up with each broker, what an authentic follow-up email says, and how you will avoid looking like another anonymous mass-blast buyer.
fields.example: Peter and Garrett skip the mass broker blast and follow up with every broker every couple of weeks in emails that sound authentic, letting the list snowball from 10 to 500 [Before You Buy or Sell a Business Podcast — Hh83Lc7sWf4 @ 00:23:59]. My cadence: 40 brokers to start, a personal note to each every fourteen days, referencing their latest listing.

fields.name: succession_pitch
fields.prompt: Write the pitch you will give an owner who distrusts outside buyers, explaining why you are the succession plan, what you will preserve, how much of your own net worth rides on the outcome, and how you differ from private equity.
fields.example: One searcher won founders who distrusted private equity by selling a portfolio of one, a promise to keep the company name, and 99.9% of personal net worth tied to the outcome [Built to Sell — GYvpRW21sSY @ 00:01:13]. My pitch: I will run only your company, keep your name on the trucks, and live or die by its results.

fields.name: outreach_infrastructure
fields.prompt: Specify your cold outreach setup, including the sending domains, mailboxes per domain, warm-up period, daily send limits by inbox provider, and how you will keep acquisition email away from your main domain to protect deliverability and reputation.
fields.example: Avi never sends cold acquisition email from the main domain, runs about 3 to 5 mailboxes per lookalike domain, and keeps Microsoft inboxes low-volume [Avi — cS2OjyHbq8U @ 00:17:26]. Warm lookalike domains for 2-3 weeks and hold Microsoft mailboxes to 5 sends per day [Avi — cS2OjyHbq8U @ 00:18:14]. My setup: three lookalike domains, four mailboxes each, three-week warm-up before the first send.

fields.name: marketplace_profile
fields.prompt: Describe how you will present yourself on online marketplaces and listing sites, including verification steps, profile links, escrow requirements, and the screening volume you will commit to, so sellers take your inquiries seriously and scammers are filtered out.
fields.example: Codie Sanchez says completing ID verification and connecting LinkedIn lifts seller response rates by more than 50% [Codie Sanchez — 3mtS8rOAqoM @ 00:44:52]. No acquisition closes without escrow, domestic or international, because it protects against scams and bad actors [acquiredotcom — nu3zh5FOFME @ 00:19:48]. My profile: verified ID and LinkedIn linked before any NDA, escrow-only offers, fifty listings reviewed monthly.

fields.name: data_accuracy_gate
fields.prompt: Define the contact-data accuracy and connect-rate thresholds you must hit before adding callers or BDRs, and describe how you will measure accuracy, track wasted rep time, and decide when your outreach engine is ready to scale.
fields.example: BDRs were wasting about 40% of their time, and fixing prospect data moved accuracy from 40% to 85%; after that, each Owner.com BDR produced over $60K closed-won ARR per month [SaaStr AI — KAz03HJ5nHg @ 00:12:09]. My gate: one caller only until a 200-record sample verifies at 85% accuracy and decision-maker connects climb above 3%.

fields.name: margin_floor_screen
fields.prompt: Set the minimum margin a target must show before you spend NDA or diligence time on it, explain why headline cash-on-cash returns cannot override that floor, and record how you will screen out businesses built on hopes.
fields.example: Codie Sanchez rejects any target below a 15% margin floor before NDA or diligence time, even when headline cash-on-cash shows 174% [Codie Sanchez — 3mtS8rOAqoM @ 00:42:09]. Her rule: do not buy other people's hopes and dreams; buy realities and profits [Codie Sanchez — 3mtS8rOAqoM @ 00:15:05]. My screen: 15% margin minimum, trailing results only, no projections counted toward price.

fields.name: seller_motive_honesty_check
fields.prompt: Write the questions you will ask about why the owner is selling, how many times you will ask them across meetings, which answers count as gut red flags about honesty, and the point at which you will walk away.
fields.example: Ask the seller why they are selling, again and again, and walk on any gut red flag about honesty [Before You Buy or Sell a Business Podcast — pqmsev-3MPY @ 00:18:48]. My rule: I ask at every meeting, log each answer word for word, and walk if the story shifts from retirement to vague industry fatigue without explanation or supporting records.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when the search model and runway months are fixed, weekly funnel counts are scheduled, broker cadence and sending domains are live, marketplace verification is complete, and written margin, data-accuracy, and seller-honesty kill criteria are signed and dated.

worksheets.title: SBA 7(a) Financing and the Seller Note Bridge
worksheets.purpose: Build a capital stack that survives the 1.25x historical coverage test, the QoE trigger, injection seasoning, and valuation review. Then structure the seller note, earnout alternatives, and personal guarantee so financing does not collapse after the LOI.
instructions: Run every coverage calculation on supported historical earnings after your own salary, never on seller projections or unverified add-backs.
Compute the business purchase price net of appraised owner-occupied real estate before deciding whether a QoE is mandatory.
Show injection sources line by line with statement dates, and attach the repayment source for any borrowed dollar.
Ask the lender to confirm the combined SBA and seller note structure before locking seller-financing terms in writing.
When a banker declines a structure, ask whether it is an SBA rule or that bank's overlay, then record the answer.

fields.name: historical_dscr_test
fields.prompt: Compute debt service coverage using only supported historical earnings after deducting your own salary, show the earnings you claimed versus what survives scrutiny, and record whether the result clears the lender floor with comfortable room to spare.
fields.example: Lenders now test 1.25x on historical financials, up from 1.15x. A seller claiming $700K that shrinks to $550K against $500K of debt service yields 1.10x and fails [Lion Business Advisors — orHTcAJcuAM @ 00:15:11]. My case: $410K supported earnings after my salary over $300K debt service is 1.37x, clearing the floor so more lenders compete.

fields.name: qoe_trigger_check
fields.prompt: Calculate the business purchase price that determines whether a quality of earnings report is mandatory, subtracting any appraised owner-occupied real estate, then record who will commission the report, the quoted fee range, and how it feeds lender underwriting.
fields.example: A $4.2M price minus $1M of real estate equals $3.2M, so a QoE is required even on a $2.7M loan [Lion Business Advisors — orHTcAJcuAM @ 00:07:05]. Quotes run $5,000 to $30,000 [Pioneer Capital Advisory LLC — WF2-6ODNQms @ 00:32:42]. My deal: $3.4M price minus $500K appraised building is $2.9M, under the trigger, but I budget a QoE because lenders read cash flow first.

fields.name: injection_build
fields.prompt: Lay out the full project cost, including working capital and fees, then show the required equity injection, how much a full-standby seller note can cover, and the exact buyer cash you must personally bring to closing.
fields.example: Exit Ready Valuation applies the 10% injection to a $1.15M project, then splits it into $57,500 of buyer cash and a $57,500 seller full-standby note [Exit Ready Valuation — Tt3Ae9PDn8A @ 00:00:54]. The 90/5/5 stack is the most common structure [Keira Hamilton — 7RAyVC1b9Pg @ 00:01:27]. My $2.2M project needs $220K: $110K cash, $110K standby note for the life of the loan.

fields.name: injection_seasoning
fields.prompt: Document where every dollar of your injection comes from, how long it has sat in your accounts, and, if any of it is borrowed through a HELOC or loan, the outside repayment source the lender will accept.
fields.example: Season the injection for two full bank statement cycles, and pair any HELOC or borrowed money with an outside repayment source such as a spouse's W-2 income [SBA Ray — 9Sl18GknuZE @ 00:04:31]. Open the HELOC before closing, while you still look strong on paper [Master Afle — LzJITHl_i2k @ 01:05:02]. Mine: $80K savings seasoned, $30K HELOC repaid from spouse's salary.

fields.name: valuation_vs_price
fields.prompt: Compare the asking price with researched market multiples before signing the LOI, and confirm that the SBA loan plus any amortizing seller note will not exceed the third-party valuation, so you avoid a forced retrade later.
fields.example: Matthias Smith says to research market multiples before the LOI, because the SBA loan plus any amortizing seller note cannot exceed the valuation, and a low appraisal forces a retrade [Matthias Smith — 3tkWRQX9WjI @ 00:14:43]. Banks are cash flow lenders, and weak cash flow usually means overpricing [Tresle Inc — NmgNpE_W_po @ 00:34:41]. My check: ask 4.2x, comps 3.8x, offer 3.8x.

fields.name: license_transfer_plan
fields.prompt: Identify every license, certification, or industry credential tied personally to the seller, name the employee or person who will qualify for it, and describe how you will bind that person to the business long after closing.
fields.example: If a license such as HVAC is tied to the seller, have an employee qualify for it and bind that employee to the business with equity or an employment agreement [SBA Ray — 9Sl18GknuZE @ 00:02:48]. My plan: the senior technician sits for the license before closing and signs a three-year employment agreement with a small equity grant.

fields.name: seller_note_structure
fields.prompt: Specify the seller note terms you will propose, including amount, standby status, whether it counts toward equity, interest rate, and how you will frame the repayment horizon so the seller accepts a long wait without feeling misled.
fields.example: A seller note counts toward equity only if it covers no more than half the required injection and sits on full standby for the life of the loan [JackQuisitions — I6M8wAaqm5s @ 00:22:18]. Never call it a 10-year note; say for the life of the loan, then pitch early payoff or refinancing after three years of returns [JackQuisitions — I6M8wAaqm5s @ 00:30:56].

fields.name: revenue_decline_stress
fields.prompt: Stress-test your combined debt load, SBA payments plus seller note payments, against a revenue decline, and record whether you can still pay both the bank and the seller while keeping coverage at or above the lender floor.
fields.example: Stress-test the seller note against a 10% revenue decline and confirm the buyer can still pay both the bank and the seller [David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB — PO1M-_wq-m4 @ 00:07:24]. My model: a 10% revenue drop cuts earnings from $410K to $345K; against $300K bank debt service plus a $20K seller payment, coverage is 1.08x, so I resize the note.

fields.name: earnout_vs_consulting
fields.prompt: Decide whether an earnout, a seller note, or a consulting agreement will bridge any valuation gap, cap the contingent payout against profit left after debt service, and write the calculation, review, and dispute process you will document.
fields.example: Roland Frasier, who prefers earnouts to notes, caps earnout payouts near half of profit left after debt service [Roland Frasier — onN8dTJIXAM @ 00:07:30]. Escamilla Law Office requires a set delivery date, records, seller review window and dispute path [Escamilla Law Office — ZGklOUqHKYg @ 00:10:27]. On SBA deals, I substitute a consulting agreement for a formal earnout, capped at $40K yearly.

fields.name: personal_guarantee_terms
fields.prompt: Record the personal guarantee terms you will negotiate, including scope, sunset period, and performance triggers, and list the pre-closing protections such as key-man insurance that you will put in place before signing any guarantee documents personally.
fields.example: Never sign the personal guarantee blind: push for partial scope, sunset clauses that burn off after 3 to 5 years, or performance triggers [Jon Stoddard — 104miMfvJRg @ 00:03:54]. When a banker pushes back, ask whether it is an SBA rule or that bank's overlay [JackQuisitions — I6M8wAaqm5s @ 00:45:19]. I bind key-man insurance before closing and request a five-year sunset.

worksheets.completion_gate: Done when historical DSCR clears 1.25x with margin after a 10% revenue stress, the QoE decision and budget are set, injection sources are seasoned and documented, the lender has confirmed the seller note structure, and personal guarantee limits are negotiated in writing.

worksheets.title: Letter of Intent Drafting and Quality of Earnings Verification
worksheets.purpose: Lock the business terms of the deal in a short, mostly non-binding letter before any diligence money is spent. Then prove which earnings are real, recurring, and transferable through proof of cash, a normalized EBITDA bridge, and a fixed-fee quality of earnings engagement that tells you whether to close, reprice, or walk.
instructions: Draft the LOI before ordering any paid report. Price, structure, payment form, working capital, timing, and closing conditions all belong in the letter, and the purchase agreement of 40 to 70 pages comes later.
Mark exclusivity and confidentiality as the binding terms. Negotiate the exclusivity window so it runs longer than your planned closing date, and write any extension triggers in black and white.
Refuse deposits and breakage fees on small deals. If a deposit is offered, specify exactly when it goes hard and deliver proof of funds before exclusivity begins.
Run proof of cash before reading any adjusted figures. Tie bank statements to the P&L and the P&L to tax returns across 36 months, and treat cash that does not match as a reason to walk.
Strike every add-back that lacks an invoice, payroll record, or genuine one-time event. Put every working capital number in a bolded written email to the seller well before closing week.

fields.name: loi_necessity_decision
fields.prompt: Decide whether this deal gets a written letter of intent before any diligence spend begins. Record what you would lose without one, including weeks of verbal negotiation and paid third-party reports, and name the afternoon on your calendar reserved to draft it.
fields.example: No LOI means no exclusivity. One buyer negotiated price verbally for three weeks, paid $8,000 for an environmental report, then lost the deal to a higher offer [Letters of Intent — VuuLz-8NiYg @ 00:00:00]. An LOI would have cost them an afternoon [Letters of Intent — VuuLz-8NiYg @ 00:00:14]. Draft date: Thursday afternoon, before ordering any reports.

fields.name: binding_terms_map
fields.prompt: List every LOI term and mark it binding or non-binding. Confirm exclusivity and confidentiality carry the binding weight, state whether any deposit is binding, and note what the seller can still do while the buyer remains committed but not bound.
fields.example: Binding: exclusivity and confidentiality only [Oberman Law Firm — 2RBitaEo6mY @ 00:05:10]. Non-binding: price, structure, payment form, working capital, timing and closing conditions. Treat exclusivity, confidentiality and deposits as binding obligations [Dean Street Law — ScOjsEfBwZQ @ 00:22:50]. After signing, the buyer is 100% committed but not 100% bound [Transact Capital — Axofinu0FSU @ 00:01:24].

fields.name: exclusivity_window
fields.prompt: Set the exclusivity length in days and compare it to your planned closing date. Write the extension triggers in black and white, explain why the seller views exclusivity as a concession, and note any board right to accept an unsolicited higher offer.
fields.example: Requesting 90 days against a 75-day planned close; exclusivity commonly runs 60 or 90 days [Brett Cenkus — aNioqOmfOe4 @ 00:02:47] and should exceed the planned close [The University of Chicago Booth School of Business — kKwXdeUVNOw @ 00:45:15]. Extension trigger: 15 days if the lender's QoE remains open. Passive investors may demand a higher-offer carve-out [KreischerMiller — Q6exObbgCgk @ 00:03:14].

fields.name: deposit_and_proof_of_funds
fields.prompt: State whether you will offer a deposit, its amount, and the exact date it goes hard. Record the proof of funds you will provide before exclusivity begins, and explain why small deals often refuse deposits and breakage fees altogether.
fields.example: No deposit on this $2.4M deal; Joel Ankney pays no deposit under $5-6M, calls a deposit request a red flag, and rejects breakage fees as mid-market creep [Joel Ankney — cl31TiHq92Y @ 00:35:06]. Proof of funds: bank statements delivered with the LOI. A $100K deposit refundable on diligence can tie a seller up with a non-buyer [Letters of Intent — VuuLz-8NiYg @ 00:18:49].

fields.name: working_capital_in_loi
fields.prompt: Decide whether the LOI states a working capital target now or defers it to the QoE. If you state one, write the dollar figure, show how a shortfall or excess moves price, and lock the lookback period used to measure it.
fields.example: Deferring the dollar target to the QoE but locking a trailing twelve-month lookback in the LOI [Transact Capital — YAk3dxgnsBU @ 00:12:57]. Reason: on a $5M target, delivering $6M pays the seller $1M more and delivering $4M cuts $1M [PCE Investment Bankers — n_gxsr8QgBM @ 00:04:31]. The LOI is a ceiling that only gets worse [Kirk Michie — QqemANnN2ZM @ 00:03:07].

fields.name: payment_structure_and_holdback
fields.prompt: Lay out the payment structure by percentage: bank debt, seller note, buyer cash, and any holdback or escrow. Specify the seller note rate, confirm it survives SBA subordination, and name what portion of price stays unpaid at closing as protection.
fields.example: 80/10/10 structure with the seller note at 8%, inside the 6 to 10% street range. Confirm the note survives SBA subordination and payment limits before it enters the LOI [Escamilla Law Office — juS-FdGX2o0 @ 00:11:56]. Never pay the full price at closing; 10% rides on a forgivable note [Dennis Unrein / SMB PE LLC — PF2SOneLrJ0 @ 00:44:55].

fields.name: buyer_entity_and_template
fields.prompt: Name the buyer entity that will sign the NDAs and LOI, and describe how it assigns to the NewCo at close. Then list what you are cutting from your LOI template, including generic praise and definitions that belong in an exhibit.
fields.example: Harbor Acquisition LLC, formed for a couple hundred dollars, signs and assigns to NewCo at close, with Section 14 cross-references checked [SMB Law Group LLP — OIcTvUbSEgM @ 00:17:14]. Generic praise stripped; one broker received 4 identical LOIs [SMB Law Group LLP — OIcTvUbSEgM @ 00:13:41]. Definitions moved to an exhibit, cutting comments about 80% [Dennis Unrein / SMB PE LLC — PF2SOneLrJ0 @ 00:38:52].

fields.name: proof_of_cash_test
fields.prompt: Run proof of cash before anything else. Tie monthly bank deposits and disbursements to the P&L, then tie the P&L to filed tax returns. Record each variance, its explanation, and whether the reconciliation covers 36 full months of bank statements.
fields.example: Deposits ran $41K below reported revenue in year two. Cash that does not match is a run signal [Acquira — g_fy5eeJpHE @ 00:06:16]. One seller booked $125,000 of revenue and receivables off a PO before invoicing [Acquira — g_fy5eeJpHE @ 00:33:13]. Two sets of books means kill or reprice, and 36 months must reconcile [Technically News — nOnsMlkLh10 @ 01:08:24].

fields.name: normalized_ebitda_bridge
fields.prompt: Build a three-column bridge from reported EBITDA through each adjustment to normalized EBITDA. For every add-back, attach the invoice, payroll record, or one-time event behind it, and reclassify any cost that recurred three years running before applying the multiple.
fields.example: Summit: $18.5M reported became $16.2M normalized, a $2.3M gap worth $23M at 10x [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — zQE4R-z6Yww @ 00:03:17]. Owner salary of $500,000 against a $350,000 replacement CEO is a $150,000 add-back [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — zQE4R-z6Yww @ 00:03:51]. Unsupported add-backs get tossed [QoE and Financial Modeling Practice — yP7oBq_gKbw @ 00:00:23].

fields.name: qoe_engagement_scope
fields.prompt: Choose the QoE provider, fee structure, and scope. Record the quoted price against the tier for this deal size, confirm the engagement is fixed-fee, and write down which outcome would trigger renegotiation versus walking away from the deal.
fields.example: Target revenue is under $2.5M, so budget $12,000-$15,000, fixed-fee so clarifying calls never generate surprise bills [Chris Barrett, CPA — 36OTOiIXSrk @ 00:02:52]. Across 50-plus deals, 45-50% came back clean, 20-25% killed the deal, and about 20% needed repricing, earnouts or seller notes [Acquira — g_fy5eeJpHE @ 00:27:49]. Walk trigger: normalized EBITDA more than 15% below the LOI basis.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete when a signed LOI names price, structure, payment form, working capital treatment, exclusivity length, and holdback; proof of cash reconciles 36 months of bank statements to the P&L and tax returns; every add-back in the normalized EBITDA bridge carries supporting documentation or has been struck; and a fixed-fee QoE engagement is signed with a written walk trigger.

worksheets.title: Add-Backs, Free Cash Flow, and the Working Capital Peg
worksheets.purpose: Separate the adjusted EBITDA that sets the price from the cash the buyer actually receives. Test each add-back, convert EBITDA to free cash flow, define and set the working capital peg from monthly history, map day-one cash, and prepare the trades and walk-away number that govern LOI negotiation.
instructions: Build your own adjusted EBITDA schedule from scratch and treat the seller's schedule only as a starting point, never a conclusion. The burden of proof on every adjustment sits with the seller.
Apply the three-question test to every add-back and flag total add-backs above 15 to 20 percent of reported EBITDA for a full forensic review.
Bridge EBITDA to free cash flow and investigate any conversion rate below 60 percent before agreeing to a multiple, splitting maintenance from growth capital spending.
Set the peg from 24 to 36 months of monthly data, never a single month, and strip seasonal peaks, one-time receivables, and accelerated collections before agreeing to a number.
Trade every concession for something specific, refuse to reprice risks disclosed up front, and write a walk-away number before negotiations start.

fields.name: three_question_addback_test
fields.prompt: Run every proposed add-back through three questions: is it truly non-recurring, will a new owner actually save it, and is it reasonable in size. Record the pass or fail for each line and the document that proves it.
fields.example: Legal fees of $38K: passed only after the invoice showed a single lawsuit settlement, per the three-question test [The Finance Lab — hIU9zSg4cQg @ 00:00:20]. Owner's truck lease: passed, since a new owner will not carry it. Annual trade-show 'one-time' cost: failed, because something that happens every year is probably normal operations [CandiMentor — QVDTq7Qd6-A @ 00:06:06].

fields.name: owner_comp_normalization
fields.prompt: Normalize owner compensation by netting the owner's pay against the market cost of a replacement manager. Record the owner's total compensation, the replacement salary, the resulting net add-back, and whether you plan to draw a lower salary yourself after closing.
fields.example: Owner draws $210K; a replacement general manager costs $95K, so the add-back is $115K, not $210K. The same logic turns a $500,000 owner salary into a $150,000 add-back [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — zQE4R-z6Yww @ 00:03:51]. Buyer salary held low in year one, with no CEO salary on day one [Walker Deibel — aoPPGxWI8dY @ 00:01:31].

fields.name: addback_threshold_check
fields.prompt: Divide total add-backs by reported EBITDA and record the percentage. If the share crosses the structural warning threshold, describe the forensic review you will run and how much enterprise value the disputed add-backs carry at your entry multiple.
fields.example: Add-backs total $290K on $1.2M reported EBITDA, about 24%, above the 15% to 20% warning line [The Finance Lab — hIU9zSg4cQg @ 00:00:59]. At 6x, every $250,000 of accepted add-backs is roughly $1.5 million of enterprise value [growthink — UfQ-Ho_j61s @ 00:03:52]. Forensic review: invoices for each line, and a fresh schedule built from scratch [The Finance Lab — hIU9zSg4cQg @ 00:01:19].

fields.name: ebitda_to_fcf_bridge
fields.prompt: Bridge normalized EBITDA down to free cash flow by subtracting maintenance capital spending, working capital build, and other cash uses. Divide free cash flow by EBITDA, record the conversion rate, and explain exactly where the cash goes if conversion falls below sixty percent.
fields.example: Normalized EBITDA $1.1M converts to $520K of free cash flow, 47%, under the 60% to 80% industrial range; Summit converted $20.7 million into $8.1 million, 39% [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — ha9dRzcYak4 @ 00:03:17]. Below 60%, locate the leak and whether it is fixable [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — ha9dRzcYak4 @ 00:08:30]. Leak here: inventory build.

fields.name: capex_maintenance_vs_growth
fields.prompt: Separate maintenance capital spending from growth spending using the twelve-month test: if all spending stopped, what breaks within a year. Request a three-year breakdown by asset category and flag any asset-heavy or capital-intensive profile that strains debt service.
fields.example: Three-year spend by category: trucks $140K, shop equipment $60K, software $25K. Trucks fail the test because routes stop within 12 months without them, so they count as maintenance [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — ha9dRzcYak4 @ 00:03:57]. Booth practitioners stay away from anything too asset or capital intensive [The University of Chicago Booth School of Business — 60ZOJolZwOo @ 00:24:42].

fields.name: nwc_definition
fields.prompt: Define exactly which accounts sit inside net working capital for the peg. List included receivables, inventory, and payables, then list items you will argue are debt instead, such as deferred revenue or accrued liabilities, and the reason for each classification.
fields.example: Included: trade receivables, inventory, trade payables. Excluded as debt-like: customer deposits and a past-due tax accrual, the kind of item more often than not thought of as debt [MCM Capital — almKwAlo5T4 @ 00:02:08]. Seller will resist; one party argues net debt to cut price, usually the buyer [Break Into Finance — S31vo0Umk5M @ 00:34:10]. Cash excluded entirely under cash-free, debt-free pricing.

fields.name: peg_lookback_and_seasonality
fields.prompt: Chart monthly net working capital across twenty-four to thirty-six months and set the peg from that history. Reject any single-month figure, strip seasonal peaks, one-time receivables, and accelerated collections, and record the resulting peg as a percentage of trailing revenue.
fields.example: Thirty months charted; NWC typically lands at 5-6% of TTM revenue, up to 15-20% [FinanceKid — 8AOvKeCdAH0 @ 00:28:44]. Here it runs 7%. Summit's NWC ranged $7.8M to $11.0M, and stripping seasonal months, a $400K insurance receivable and $600K of accelerated collections explained a $900K peg gap [John Colley | The Investment Banking Practitioner — x_72u8PgHpc @ 00:06:34].

fields.name: true_up_mechanics_and_escrow
fields.prompt: Write the post-closing true-up process: who delivers the closing statement, how many days after close, how the seller reviews it, and how disputes resolve. Size the escrow or holdback so a working capital shortfall is absorbed without touching the seller note.
fields.example: Buyer delivers the closing statement within 90 days, inside the 60 to 120 day norm [A Simple Model — C-seCQXqtM4 @ 00:01:47]. A $200,000 holdback absorbs shortfalls, $100,000 pulled from it [FinanceKid — 8AOvKeCdAH0 @ 00:08:56]. No set-off against the seller note for working capital, since set-off does not solve today's cash shortage [SMB Law Group LLP — iNOj__jXGpE @ 00:11:52].

fields.name: day_one_cash_map
fields.prompt: Map every cash obligation due in the first weeks after closing against expected collection dates. Identify the gap, state whether the seller leaves enough cash or a revolver or overdraft covers it, and confirm the agreed amount in a bolded written email.
fields.example: Payroll and rent hit $118K in week one while collections arrive in week four, so the seller leaves cash or a revolver goes in place immediately [Break Into Finance — S31vo0Umk5M @ 00:57:05]. The number is bolded in writing; one seller agreed to $750,000 in a presentation, then insisted on $150,000 two days before closing [Acquira — g_fy5eeJpHE @ 00:38:03].

fields.name: loi_trades_and_walkaway
fields.prompt: List each concession the seller requests and the specific item you will demand in exchange. Write your pre-set walk-away price, and describe how you will handle late repricing, including the specific new finding required to justify any change.
fields.example: We want 90-day exclusivity; the seller will ask for a faster diligence list or an escrow deposit in exchange [MySaasForSale — OOlka50xFck @ 00:03:06]. Walk-away: $3.1M. Any retrade must cite a specific new finding, never a risk disclosed up front [MySaasForSale — OOlka50xFck @ 00:05:36]. Price is the only lever we control [Technically News — nOnsMlkLh10 @ 00:30:45].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete when every add-back has a documented pass or fail result, total add-backs are measured against reported EBITDA, the EBITDA-to-free-cash-flow bridge shows a conversion rate with an explanation, the peg is defined account by account from monthly history, true-up and holdback terms are written, day-one cash is mapped, and a walk-away price is recorded.

worksheets.title: Deal Structure, Buyer Protections, and the First 100 Days
worksheets.purpose: Choose the asset or stock structure, write the tax treatment and allocation into the deal, and protect the buyer with personal indemnities and a matched seller note. Then stabilize cash, people, customers, and controls through the first 100 days before accelerating anything, so the business survives the ownership change intact.
instructions: Default to an asset purchase unless a specific reason justifies stock, and write the tax path into the LOI instead of leaving it silent.
Negotiate the Form 8594 allocation and the down payment together, and confirm both parties will file matching figures with the IRS.
Have every selling shareholder sign the indemnity personally, size the seller note to match the indemnity cap, and clear every consent and license before closing.
Put dual bank signatures in place by Day 15 and a 13-week cash forecast live by week two, with the approver and the sender of payments always different people.
Stabilize before you accelerate: freeze big, hard-to-reverse changes, tell employees before customers, keep marketing active, and stress-test the plan for a 5 to 10 percent revenue dip.

fields.name: asset_vs_stock_choice
fields.prompt: Choose asset purchase or stock purchase and justify it. Record the seller's preference and why, the liabilities you avoid or inherit under each structure, the extra diligence a stock deal demands, and what the seller concedes to accept your structure.
fields.example: Asset purchase. The seller wants stock so they are done at close, while buyers want assets to choose what to take and avoid unknown liabilities [Chris Barsness - Securities Law Media — -DthgkqGsGA @ 00:01:57]. Almost all main street deals close as asset sales anyway [Walker Deibel — NM-ZwBNBHQE @ 00:02:06]. Concession offered: slightly higher price to offset the seller's tax cost.

fields.name: tax_structure_in_loi
fields.prompt: Write the tax structure into the LOI rather than leaving it silent. Name the path, whether asset purchase, 338(h)(10), 336(e), or F reorganization, note the 80% stock threshold where relevant, and record whether the seller is a standalone C Corp.
fields.example: LOI names the F reorg path and addresses the 80% stock threshold instead of leaving tax silent [Dennis Unrein / SMB PE LLC — hDmKsEVGoBI @ 00:01:23]. Goal: a stepped-up basis, since $1M of intangibles amortizes over 15 years, while $1M bought as stock stays trapped in basis until exit [Tax Hack Accounting Group — Wd1__Z4Nz6k @ 00:02:32].

fields.name: form_8594_allocation
fields.prompt: Draft the purchase price allocation by asset class for Form 8594 and confirm both sides will file matching figures. Negotiate the allocation together with the down payment, recording how much goodwill the seller note spreads and how inventory is treated.
fields.example: Allocation: inventory $180K, equipment $220K, goodwill $1.6M. Inventory is ineligible for installment reporting, so the seller wants it covered by cash at close, and the seller note only spreads goodwill [Hans Goldstein: Tax & Exit Planning — I8L23gqP5to @ 00:02:57]. Both returns must match or the IRS will probably catch it [Teach Me! Personal Finance — G0f0r8tYMnk @ 00:05:35].

fields.name: indemnity_and_seller_note
fields.prompt: Set the indemnity cap, deductible, and survival period, then size the seller note to match the cap. Name every selling shareholder who signs the indemnity personally, and describe how set-off against the note works for breaches of representations and warranties.
fields.example: Cap 12%, deductible 0.75%, survival 18 months, within the 10-15% cap, 0.5-1% deductible and 12-24 month norms [SMB Law Group LLP — iNOj__jXGpE @ 00:26:54]. Seller note sized at 12% to match. Both owners sign personally, or the company empties its cash after closing and the claim is worthless [SMB Law Group LLP — iNOj__jXGpE @ 00:19:51]. Set-off applies to rep breaches.

fields.name: consents_and_licenses
fields.prompt: List every change-of-control clause, lease, landlord consent, and non-transferable license that must clear before closing. For each, record the counterparty, the deadline, and the backup plan if a license is tied to the seller personally rather than the business.
fields.example: Every change-of-control clause and the landlord consent on the shop lease must clear before closing [Chris Barsness - Securities Law Media — -DthgkqGsGA @ 00:06:31]. The HVAC license sits with the seller, so a senior technician qualifies for it and is bound by an employment agreement [SBA Ray — 9Sl18GknuZE @ 00:02:48]. Deadline for both: ten days before closing.

fields.name: cash_controls_by_day_15
fields.prompt: Set the first financial controls after closing: dual signatures on every bank account, separation between whoever approves payments and whoever sends them, and a 13-week cash forecast. Record target dates, owners, and the variance threshold that triggers a written explanation.
fields.example: Dual signatures on every account by Day 15 and the 13-week forecast live by week two [Lighthouse Capital — OwAOc9xgv9U @ 00:01:07]. Red flag: a gap above 10% for two consecutive weeks [Lighthouse Capital — OwAOc9xgv9U @ 00:00:51]. The office manager approves and the new owner sends, never the same person [Lighthouse Capital — OwAOc9xgv9U @ 00:01:38].

fields.name: first_100_days_stabilization
fields.prompt: Write the stabilization plan for days 1 through 100. List which personnel, pricing, and process changes are frozen, for how long, which questions you will ask the local controller first, and what evidence by Day 100 proves the close is under control.
fields.example: Personnel changes frozen six months, changes kept incremental [Technically News — nOnsMlkLh10 @ 00:58:06]. Before Friday, request the last bank reconciliation for every account, the oldest suspense item, and what the controller would fix first [Neo Expertise — 4kQ8R30J5q4 @ 00:02:14]. Day 100 proof: month-end close of 10 business days or less for three straight months [Lighthouse Capital — OwAOc9xgv9U @ 00:01:55].

fields.name: revenue_dip_stress_test
fields.prompt: Stress-test the first-year P&L for a post-closing revenue decline. Model a five percent dip and a full ten percent drop, then confirm you can still pay both the bank and the seller note while keeping debt service coverage at or above 1.25.
fields.example: Revenue fell 5-10% in the year after each of seven acquisitions [Walker Deibel — fFDPLnXTi0o @ 00:06:22]. At a 10% decline, cash flow drops from $520K to $430K against $330K of combined bank and seller payments, about 1.30x, so both still get paid [David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB — PO1M-_wq-m4 @ 00:07:24].

fields.name: customer_and_market_communication
fields.prompt: Sequence the announcement: employees first, then customers, then the market. List the top paying customers you will visit personally, any client above twenty percent concentration, and the weekly marketing activity that keeps lead flow from going dark after the press release.
fields.example: Employees told first, then the top 20 paying customers booked for visits [Let's Buy a Business — WP5MdYhV05A @ 00:16:59]. Largest client: 18% of sales, so a voice-of-customer tour runs first [Patrick O'Connell - M&A Transaction Services — 6AT45jrM2CU @ 00:25:49]. Going dark cost one firm 40% of lead flow in three weeks [Strategy Leaders Inc. — OeJwN9bz5dE @ 00:12:31].

fields.name: retention_and_knowledge_capture
fields.prompt: Name the key employees whose knowledge the business depends on and describe how you will capture it and keep them. Record the interview schedule, the SOPs you expect to produce, and who funds any retention or thank-you bonuses, on what schedule.
fields.example: Dispatcher and lead estimator each get two recorded 90-minute interviews, converted into SOPs and FAQs [Patrick O'Connell - M&A Transaction Services — 6AT45jrM2CU @ 00:23:24]. The seller pays thank-you bonuses, half now and half escrowed for 12 months, which we match if needed [The Intentional Owner — cC2-F0YZb9M @ 00:28:53]. Seller-funded bonuses avoid signaling the buyer is flush.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete when the structure and tax path are written into the LOI, the Form 8594 allocation is agreed with the seller, indemnity terms and the matching seller note are documented with every shareholder signing personally, all consents and licenses are cleared, cash controls are live by Day 15, and the 100-day plan survives a 10 percent revenue decline stress test.
